2610.06670.title: Reward Stealing Attack on Large Language Models
2610.06670.paper_summary: Adversarial attacks on Large Language Models (LLMs) aim to induce harmful content. However, existing methods suffer from high computational costs or strict model-pairing dependencies, limiting their scalability and transferability. We propose Reward Stealing Attack (ReSA), an adversarial attack framework that targets the latent safety reward underlying LLM alignment. ReSA employs maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning to recover a proxy reward model solely from the aligned model's behavior. The extracted reward is then reversed at inference time to derive an adversarial policy, efficiently implemented via a reward-guided decoding mechanism. Experiments demonstrate that a single recovered reward generalizes across prompts and diverse models to reveal a fundamental alignment vulnerability, enabling ReSA to significantly outperform existing attacks in effectiveness and transferability. The code is available at https://github.com/GarminQ/ReSA.
2610.06670.paper_summary_zh: 對大型語言模型（LLMs）的對抗攻擊旨在引發有害內容。<lb/>然而，現有的方法面臨高計算成本或嚴格的模型配對依賴性，限制了其可擴展性和可轉移性。<lb/>我們提出了獎勵竊取攻擊（ReSA），這是一種針對LLM對齊背後潛在安全獎勵的對抗攻擊框架。<lb/>ReSA採用最大熵逆強化學習，僅根據對齊模型的行為來恢復代理獎勵模型。<lb/>提取的獎勵在推理時被反轉，以推導出對抗策略，通過獎勵引導的解碼機制高效實現。<lb/>實驗表明，單一恢復的獎勵在提示和不同模型之間具有泛化能力，揭示了基本的對齊脆弱性，使ReSA在有效性和可轉移性上顯著超越現有攻擊。<lb/>代碼可在 https://github.com/GarminQ/ReSA 獲得。
